module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 973

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/973](https://www.erdosproblems.com/973)
- [Er92f] Erdős, L., On some problems of {P}. Turán concerning power sums of
  complex numbers. Acta Math. Hungar. (1992), 11--24.
- [Ha74] Hayman, W. K., Research problems in function theory: new problems. (1974), 155--180.
- [LYZ26] Luo, Yanping and Yang, Ruiyi and Zhu, Keheng, Exterior power sums.
  [arxiv/2607.22017](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22017)
- [Tu84b] Turán, Paul, On a new method of analysis and its applications. (1984), xvi+584.
-/

@[expose] public section

open Finset Filter

namespace Erdos973

/--
Does there exist a constant $C>1$ such that, for every $n\geq 2$, there exists a sequence
$z_i\in \mathbb{C}$ with $z_1=1$ and $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$ for all $1\leq i\leq n$ with
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert < C^{-n}$?

This is Problem 7.3 in [Ha74], where it is attributed to Erdős.

The answer is no, by Luo, Yang and Zhu [LYZ26]: the maximum exceeds $e^{-\lambda n}$ for every
fixed $\lambda>0$ once $n$ is large, so it decays subexponentially and no such $C$ exists. See
`erdos_973.variants.luo_yang_zhu` below.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973 :
    answer(False) ↔
      ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧
        ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
          z 1 = 1 ∧
          (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) ∧
          (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
The result of [LYZ26] that settles the problem: for every fixed $\lambda>0$ and all large enough
$n$, any $z_1,\dots,z_n$ with $\lvert z_j\rvert\geq 1$ satisfy
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert\sum_j z_j^k\right\rvert > e^{-\lambda n}$.

This is sharper than `erdos_973.variants.tang`, whose bound $(2e)^{-(1+o(1))n}$ pins the rate at
$\log(2e) = 1 + \log 2$, still exponential decay.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.luo_yang_zhu (lam : ℝ) (hlam : 0 < lam) :
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ z : ℕ → ℂ,
      (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) →
      ∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1),
        Real.exp (-lam * n) < ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ := by
  sorry

/--
Erdős proved (as described on p.35 of [Tu84b]) that such a sequence does exist with
$\lvert z_i\rvert\leq 1$. Indeed, Erdős' construction gives a value of $C\approx 1.32$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.le_one :
    ∃ C : ℝ, C > 1 ∧
      ∀ n : ℕ, n ≥ 2 → ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
        z 1 = 1 ∧
        (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z i‖ ≤ 1) ∧
        (∀ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ < C ^ (-(n : ℝ))) := by
  sorry

/--
In [Er92f] (a different) Erdős refines this analysis, proving that if
$M_2=\min_{z_j} \max_{2\leq k\leq n+1} \left\lvert \sum_{1\leq j\leq n}z_j^k\right\rvert$
where the minimum is taken over all $z_j\in \mathbb{C}$ with $\max \lvert z_j\rvert=1$, then
$(1.746)^{-n} < M_2 < (1.745)^{-n}$ for all sufficiently large $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.m2_bounds :
    ∀ᶠ n : ℕ in atTop, ∀ M_2 : ℝ,
      IsGLB { M | ∃ z : ℕ → ℂ,
        (∀ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ ≤ 1) ∧
        (∃ j ∈ Icc 1 n, ‖z j‖ = 1) ∧
        (∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), M = ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ k‖ ∧
          ∀ m ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1), ‖∑ j ∈ Icc 1 n, z j ^ m‖ ≤ M) } M_2 →
      (1.746 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) < M_2 ∧ M_2 < (1.745 : ℝ) ^ (-(n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

/--
Tang notes in the comments that Theorem 6.1 of [Tu84b] implies that, if $\lvert z_i\rvert \geq 1$
for all $i$, then
$\max_{2\leq k\leq n+1}\left\lvert \sum_{1\leq i\leq n}z_i^k\right\rvert \geq (2e)^{-(1+o(1))n}$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_973.variants.tang :
    ∃ f : ℕ → ℝ, f =o[atTop] (fun _ ↦ (1 : ℝ)) ∧
    ∀ᶠ n in atTop, ∀ z : ℕ → ℂ,
      (∀ i ∈ Icc 1 n, 1 ≤ ‖z i‖) →
      ∃ k ∈ Icc 2 (n + 1),
        ‖∑ i ∈ Icc 1 n, z i ^ k‖ ≥
        (2 * Real.exp 1) ^ (-(1 + f n) * (n : ℝ)) := by
  sorry

end Erdos973

findings.description: The explanation at lines 46–47 says that the maximum “decays subexponentially.” The cited lower bound rules out exponential decay; it does not establish decay to zero. For an arbitrary admissible configuration, the maximum need not decay at all: taking every z_i = 1 gives maximum n. Even for the optimal maximum, the cited paper explicitly leaves open whether it stays bounded away from zero. The Lean theorem and its negative answer are faithful; only this explanatory wording overstates the conclusion.
findings.source_evidence: Luo–Yang–Zhu, Exterior Power Sums, arXiv:2607.22017v1, final remark in Section 4: “It remains open within the present argument whether these quantities are bounded away from zero or decay on a subexponential, for example polynomial, scale.” Theorem 1.1 establishes the uniform exponential lower bounds and the nth-root limits. https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.22017
findings.suggested_fix: Replace “so it decays subexponentially” with “so the optimal maximum cannot decay exponentially,” retaining the conclusion that no such C exists.

reformulations.difference: Instead of defining the attained minimum M₂, Lean universally quantifies over real numbers satisfying IsGLB for the set of attainable power-sum maxima, and asserts the bounds conditionally on that property.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n ≥ 1, the two norm conditions express exactly max_j |z_j| = 1, and the equality at one exponent together with the bounds at every exponent expresses exactly the finite maximum. The admissible finite-dimensional domain is nonempty and compact, and the objective is continuous, so its infimum is attained; Er92f explicitly notes this compactness argument on p. 11. Consequently its unique greatest lower bound is precisely the source's minimum. The use of sequences on ℕ adds only unused coordinates. Scratch Lean proofs establish nonemptiness, boundedness below, existence of the GLB, and the equivalence of the conditional formulation with bounds on sInf. The full compactness/attainment identification was checked mathematically, not formalized.

review.notes: All five Lean statements match the recovered mathematical sources. Scratch files /workspace/review/scratch.lean and /workspace/review/boundary.lean check the interval boundaries, real-power and little-o meanings, GLB nonvacuity, finite-maximum formulations, and the implication from the LYZ bound to the negative answer. An exact n=2 witness works with C=11/10 and z₂=(5+12i)/13. Live erdosproblems.com requests were blocked; the recovered July archive predates the LYZ paper, and the auxiliary database's open-status entry was last updated in 2025. Neither establishes a current status conflict, so none is reported. The original Ha74 and Tu84b texts were not retrieved directly; their relevant claims were checked through the archived problem page, the newer Hayman edition, and the other primary papers.
